idea: Annotation-only NSRR fallback: hypnogram strings + event tokens as text for the existing GRPO loop
how_it_works: Each SHHS/MESA night becomes one text record: a covariate header (age, sex, BMI, site) followed by the 30s stage sequence from the NSRR profusion XML (W/N1/N2/N3/R, ~1000 tokens per night, run-length compressed to ~150) with interleaved event tokens from ScoredEvents (arousal, obstructive/central apnea, hypopnea, SpO2 desat with nadir bucket) positioned at their epoch index. The frozen text LLM gets three RL tasks with cheap verifiable rewards: (1) next-K-epoch stage prediction scored by macro-F1 against the label file, (2) OSA severity class (AHI <5/5-15/15-30/>30) from the harmonized CSV, scored by ordinal accuracy, and (3) an attacker policy that inserts or deletes a bounded number of event tokens to flip a frozen classifier's severity call, rewarded only if the edited night still passes a plausibility check (event density and stage-transition statistics within cohort quantiles). GRPO samples 8 to 16 completions per night, rewards are pure Python over strings, so the loop needs no signal preprocessing and runs on one GPU. Headline experiment: train on SHHS1 (~5800 nights), evaluate zero-shot on MESA (~2000 nights, different demographics and scoring center), reporting severity accuracy and stage-prediction F1 against a logistic-regression-on-stage-statistics baseline. Full cohorts fit in memory since annotation files total under 1 GB.
load_bearing_risk: AHI leakage. AHI in the covariate CSV is computed directly from the respiratory events in the same XML, so task (2) with event tokens present is a counting problem and any model will look excellent. The honest headline must predict severity from stages plus arousals only (events masked), and the attacker task must target a classifier trained on the masked view. If reviewers spot unmasked events, the paper is dead.
first_concrete_step: Write nsrr_to_text.py: parse one SHHS profusion XML with xml.etree, emit a JSON line {id, covariates, stages: 'W W N1 N2 ...', events: [(epoch, type, duration, desat_nadir)]}, then join to shhs1-harmonized-dataset.csv on nsrrid and assert that recomputed AHI from events matches the CSV within 10 percent on 50 nights. That assertion both validates the parser and proves the leakage path exists, forcing the masked-view design before any training runs.
sub_ideas: Masked-event pretraining: train the LLM to reconstruct deleted event tokens from stage context alone (BERT-style over hypnograms), then fine-tune with GRPO. Gives a signal-free pretrained sleep-event LM and a natural ablation.

Cross-cohort scoring-shift detection: MESA and SHHS used different scoring rules (AASM 2007 vs R&K, 3 vs 4 percent desat). Reward the model for predicting the cohort from the annotation text and use the confidence as a domain-shift metric, which turns the SHHS->MESA drop into a quantified, explainable result rather than a mystery.

Outcome prediction from hypnogram text: SHHS has linked mortality and CVD outcomes. Same serialization, reward = correct 10-year CVD event label. Prior hypnogram-outcome papers used hand features, so an LLM-RL result is a clean comparison and a bridge to the workshop's foundation-model framing.

Attacker-as-scoring-audit: instead of fooling a model, reward the attacker for minimal edits that move a night across an AHI threshold, then histogram which edit types suffice. This surfaces which nights are clinically fragile to scorer disagreement and is a defensible use of the adversarial machinery.

Bridge to raw signals later: if the EDF tokenizer recovers, its output tokens slot into the same text record as an extra channel. The annotation pipeline becomes the label and prompt scaffold for the full system, so hours spent here are not wasted.
